assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling turned aryl amine synthesis into a routine, general operation. The ligand-controlled Buchwald-Hartwig amination is used daily in medicinal and process chemistry, and its practical conceptual simplicity is what I value most in a method.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, ligand-enabled general version in the mid-1990s and then drove generations of ligand design. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work was a stoichiometric-tin precursor and is better treated as historical context than as a third laureate.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of independent adoption in pharma, agrochemicals and materials, with commercial ligand families. Fully mature. The main timing issue is that Pd cross-coupling was recognized in 2010, so the committee may ask whether this is a distinct enough advance.
uncertainties: How much novelty the committee sees relative to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Precise priority between early Migita/Kosugi tin amide chemistry and the Buchwald and Hartwig catalytic systems (I am working from memory).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization changes retrosynthetic logic by treating ubiquitous C-H bonds as functional groups. Ligand- and directing-group-controlled Pd catalysis, together with Ir-catalyzed borylation, has enabled late-stage functionalization and shorter step counts, which is exactly the efficiency theme in synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Yu is the clearest owner of ligand-accelerated, template-controlled and distal C-H activation. Sanford made key contributions to Pd(II)/Pd(IV) catalysis and oxidative functionalization. Hartwig's contribution (Ir borylation, alkane functionalization) overlaps with other candidates. Daugulis and Smith are also credible, so a three-person cut is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted in discovery chemistry and total synthesis, with industrial uptake still growing. Selectivity for arbitrary substrates and practical scale are not fully solved, so the field is somewhat younger than cross-coupling.
uncertainties: The split between directing-group, ligand-enabled and borylation contributions makes the three-person configuration unstable.
Industrial-scale use is less established than for cross-coupling.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a general mode of single-electron radical bond formation under mild conditions, and it is now routine in synthesis labs. It expanded the reaction toolbox, including dual catalysis with nickel, and is being adopted in industry and flow processes.
assessment.attribution: The 2008-2009 reports by MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson were close in time and independently important. Nicewicz, König, Fukuzumi and Melchiorre also contributed substantially, and the Ru/Ir photocatalyst background predates all of them. MacMillan received the 2021 prize for organocatalysis, which may weigh against him.
assessment.maturity: Very rapid adoption and strong independent confirmation. Timing is reasonable, but the history is crowded and the foundational photochemistry predates the synthetic turn.
uncertainties: Crowded credit and a prior prize for one candidate laureate.
Whether the committee sees this as a new concept or an extension of earlier photochemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolable stable carbenes overturned the belief that free carbenes were only transient. N-heterocyclic carbenes became ubiquitous ligands, for example in Grubbs-type metathesis catalysts, and organocatalysts, and they redefined main-group bonding concepts. That is a clear what-was-new-chemically story.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo isolated the crystalline imidazol-2-ylidene in 1991, and Bertrand reported stable phosphinocarbenes in 1988 that showed carbene stability. Wanzlick's earlier work is historical context. Nolan, Rovis and Bode applied NHCs in catalysis, but the foundational credit is the two isolations.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of confirmation and broad impact across catalysis, so it is mature, possibly overdue. A clean two-person attribution is a plus.
uncertainties: Weighting of Bertrand's 1988 carbenes versus Arduengo's 1991 NHC (from memory).
Applications belong partly to catalysis breakthroughs already recognized in 2005.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides, making total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins practical. This is a genuine new reaction that has changed how proteins are made and modified, from synthetic proteins to site-specific modification.
assessment.attribution: The 1994 paper was by Dawson, Muir, Clark-Lewis and Kent. Kent led the ligation concept, and Muir's expressed protein ligation extended it to semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu developed important extensions, so the credit set is somewhat contested beyond the three names.
assessment.maturity: About 30 years of independent adoption and many synthetic proteins. It is mature, though the scale of true synthetic protein production is still limited.
uncertainties: Whether the chemistry or the biology applications drive the committee's view.
Allocation of credit among ligation-extension contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made reliable solid-phase oligonucleotide synthesis possible and is the foundation of PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide therapeutics. It is a case where a better reaction enabled a whole technology, with very high daily-use impact.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers is the principal inventor of the phosphoramidite method. Hood is credited in connection with automated synthesis instrumentation, which is a separate, more engineering-oriented contribution, so I propose Caruthers alone.
assessment.maturity: Developed in the early 1980s with decades of near-universal use, so it is extremely mature and perhaps long overdue, although the sole-laureate configuration may be seen as thin.
uncertainties: Credit for Letsinger's earlier phosphite-triester chemistry is not represented in the supplied names (from memory).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically hindered acid-base pairs can heterolytically activate H2 and other small molecules without metals. This is a conceptual and chemical novelty with applications in metal-free hydrogenation.
assessment.attribution: Stephan reported the first metal-free reversible H2 activation in 2006 and Erker contributed key related systems. Two-person credit is clean from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: About twenty years of confirmation and growing use, but practical impact on synthesis is smaller than for the broad methods above, so it may still be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Real-world uptake in synthesis and industry is limited compared with transition-metal catalysis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation via PROTACs and molecular glues is a new pharmacological mode built from chemistry, with strong clinical momentum. As a synthetic chemist I would ask what is new chemically, and the answer is mainly in design principles for heterobifunctional molecules rather than a new reaction.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched PROTACs in 2001, Ciulli introduced VHL-based and structural design principles, and thalidomide-cereblon work (Handa, Ito) provides the molecular-glue side. This compound discovery has two parts that may need different recognition, and the configuration is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Recent and rapidly maturing, with many clinical-stage degraders but no fully approved PROTAC drug that I can confirm. May be premature for a prize.
uncertainties: Premature relative to the older candidates above.
Unclear division between PROTAC and molecular-glue credit.
